clue.text: The public funds that used to be provided for delinquents?

definitions.text: used to be provided for delinquents

explanation.surface: A note on how public money was once spent on young offenders.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the second sense: the 'provision' for delinquents was a punishment frame, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Government stocks are public funds; the old wooden stocks were a pillory where offenders were locked and pelted.

clue.text: Checks returned in batches?

explanation.surface: Cheques bounced back by the bank in bundles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' tempts the reader towards bank cheques returned in bundles; it means hindrances, and the second half plays on SET (batch) and BACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Checks are reverses or hindrances; read as two words, sets (batches) that are backs (returned) describe items sent back in groups.

clue.text: Round coin detectives brought into the West

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: brought into says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police officers bring a coin round to the West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is a formal name for the Western world, the opposite of the Orient.

clue.text: Malayan cutter

parts.note: read as a blade from Malaya rather than a boat or a person who cuts

explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a wavy-bladed Malay dagger, a cutting weapon from that region.

clue.text: The Indian songbird 14's gardener brought round in a tank

indicators.note: in says the turned name sits inside the other letters

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquid

indicators.note: brought round says the gardener's name is turned to face the other way

parts.note: 14 across is the garden of Genesis, whose gardener was Adam

explanation.surface: An Indian bird is carried by a gardener inside a water tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' reverses ADAM to MADA, and 'in' places it inside A VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The amadavat, or red avadavat, is a small finch kept as a cage songbird in India.

clue.text: Aurora seen tripping joyously round the maypole?

definitions.text: seen tripping joyously round the maypole

explanation.surface: Villagers dancing happily round a maypole at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aurora' looks like a goddess of dawn or a girl's name; it is the northern lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern lights are called the merry dancers in Scotland; literally, it describes cheerful dancers at a maypole.

clue.text: Handy device for the clerk who wishes to mark time

definitions.text: Handy device for the clerk who wishes to mark time

parts.words: Handy device for the clerk who wishes to mark time
parts.note: to mark time here means to print the day on a document, not to wait idly

explanation.definitionFit: An office tool inks the day's calendar entry onto letters and forms.

clue.text: Food eaten from divans, maybe

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of the word could be put in another order

explanation.surface: Snacks eaten while lounging on sofas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten from' joins the pieces; 'maybe' rearranges DIVANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Viands is an old word for provisions or dishes of meat.

clue.text: Having a shot at judicial work?

explanation.surface: A lawyer attempting a career in the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: To be attempting something is to give it a go; a judge hearing a case is said to be hearing it in court.

clue.text: Northerner retreating in alarm

indicators.note: retreating says the word goes backwards

parts.note: a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A Scotsman backs away in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is a warning bell or alarm signal.

clue.text: A dry fellow held back by the waves on the coast of France

indicators.note: held says the sea word holds the turned letters

parts.note: the briny is a name for the sea

indicators.note: back says the short run of letters is turned around

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who keeps off drink

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is kept from shore by the waves off the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A TT into TTA, and 'held' puts it inside BRINY.
explanation.definitionFit: This region is the peninsula of north-west France with a long Atlantic coastline.

clue.text: Britain's flow of capital personified

parts.note: the flow is a river through the capital, London, pictured as a bearded old man, not money moving

explanation.definitionFit: The river through London is traditionally shown as a venerable figure in statues and cartoons.

clue.text: His military role is to give general assistance

definitions.text: His military role is to give general assistance

parts.words: His military role is to give general assistance
parts.note: general assistance reads as all-round help but means help for a general

explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is an officer who assists a senior commander.

clue.text: Russian girl coming from the bank at Yalta

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Russian girl arrives from the shore at the Crimean resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Katya is a common Russian girl's name, a familiar form of Ekaterina.

clue.text: Perfectly good original plot

parts.note: plot reads as a story line but means a patch of ground, the first one, where all was good

explanation.definitionFit: The garden of Genesis was the first paradise, a sinless piece of land.

clue.text: Doctor given tea for coffee

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A doctor is served tea instead of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine coffee originally shipped from a Yemeni port.

clue.text: See 6
Asking for the wrong card from the pack

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at a card table requests the wrong card.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the court cards in the red suit of a standard deck.

clue.text: A salmon I made a fine picture of in Paris

indicators.note: made says the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: An artist boasts of painting a fish while in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges A SALMON I. 'of in Paris' links and hints at the Louvre, where the painting hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait is perhaps the most famous painting in the world.

clue.text: She is provided with a different label at the finish

indicators.note: at the finish says the reworked letters go at the end
different says the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman finds a new label stuck on her at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns LABEL into BELLA, placed after IS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a woman's name, so it stands for any female person.

clue.text: Little films about ordinary emergency rations, perhaps

indicators.note: about says one word goes around the other

parts.note: shorts are brief films
common means ordinary

explanation.surface: Short movies about everyday emergency supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on scant fare means having too little food, as with reduced rations.

clue.text: An expert who brings science to the art of government?

definitions.text: An expert who brings science to the art of government

parts.words: An expert who brings science to the art of government
parts.note: a scientist advising politicians, the backroom researcher of wartime Whitehall

explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word names a scientific expert, especially one doing research for the state.

clue.text: A chirpy six-footer, not a gentleman in the American secret service

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A tall cheerful spy who is no gentleman works for American intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect has six legs and makes a loud chirping noise.

clue.text: The god of love and discord?

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scores, the letter O
a din is a discordant racket

explanation.surface: A question about which deity rules love and strife.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: A youngster fleeced before reaching maturity

definitions.text: A youngster fleeced before reaching maturity

parts.words: A youngster fleeced before reaching maturity
parts.note: fleeced reads as cheated but means sheared of its wool, and the youngster is a young sheep

explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep that has had its coat cut off, proverbially tempered against the wind.

clue.text: See 24
See 27
Sea-girt bird sanctuary in which a rifle is out of place

indicators.note: out of place says the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A gun is unwelcome at a bird reserve on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: This Shetland island is a noted seabird haven surrounded by ocean.

clue.text: Appalling change from ease

indicators.note: change says the letters are switched into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Going from comfort to something dreadful is a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frightening and terrible to face is appalling.

clue.text: Idle travesty about an Old Testament prophet

indicators.note: about says the reworked letters go round the other piece
a travesty is a distorted version, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A mocking parody of a biblical seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travesty' rearranges IDLE to DIEL, and 'about' puts it around AN.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Hebrew prophet of the lions' den.

clue.text: A trap set outside regions in which the U.S. has vital interests

definitions.text: in which the U.S. has vital interests

indicators.note: set outside says the trap word is placed around the other

parts.note: a net is a trap
areas are regions

explanation.surface: Laying a trap beyond zones that matter to American policy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern lands around the eastern Mediterranean have long been central to American foreign policy.

clue.text: Secrets a painter is able to conceal

indicators.note: to conceal says the painter hides the other piece inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
can means is able

explanation.surface: An artist manages to keep secrets hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are mysteries or hidden knowledge.
